report: PR #16 reproduces a real cancellation timing defect in Chromium: the jump buffer for level-one barrier l1-o1 launches before the safe right-lane input, so this must remain a failure. WebKit executes the same branch with the lane input at the buffer timestamp and clears l1-o1 without a jump; that passing browser result does not close Chromium coverage.

scope.rationale: The defect is in a gameplay input/state-machine branch and the observed event ordering differs across Chromium and WebKit. Keep the issue on the formal QA retest path; the root cause is not established by these artifacts.

steps: Start a fresh level-one replay at the default 390x844 portrait viewport.
Wait until the jump control is visible and ready.
Use the browser touch API on the visible jump control, followed immediately by the visible right-lane control, with no state injection.
Read the live event history after the game advances beyond the l1-o1 barrier.
observed: Chromium: l1-o1 buffers at 18.0159 game seconds / 135.11925 m; jump launches at 18.2742 / 137.0565 m; lane input to lane 2 arrives at 18.3993 / 137.99475 m. The later barrier-clear event is unjumped; the check correctly fails because launch preceded lane input.
WebKit: l1-o1 buffers and lane-input to lane 2 are both recorded at 17.34 / 130.05 m; the barrier clears unjumped at 18.803 / 141.0225 m, with no jump event.
Chromium cancel-jump-safe-detour.png was captured after the report snapshot already contains the jump event; its HUD shows about 154 m. It is post-launch evidence, not proof of cancellation.
The recorded controls use public Playwright touchscreen.tap actions and normalInputOnly=true; the browser event isTrusted flag was not separately recorded.

acceptanceCriteria: On the exact level-one l1-o1 barrier branch, a trusted touch lane-change input received before jump launch clears the pending buffer before any jump event is emitted.

In both Chromium and WebKit at the declared 390x844 portrait viewport, the normal-input trace shows jump-buffered followed by the safe lane change, no jump event, bufferedJump=null, and l1-o1 clearing with jumped=false.

The cancelled action adds no jumped-barrier count, jump mastery/star progress, or jump reward; compare progress against the pre-branch save so prior earned mastery is not erased or mistaken for a new award.

Capture the branch with real touch input and player-visible evidence; record the event ordering and the exact engine/viewport. A post-launch screenshot or a passing sibling engine cannot satisfy the Chromium criterion.
